the-flight-simulator-strategy.core: Pilots train for emergencies in simulators so real ones feel familiar. Mock interviews do the same: they rehearse thinking aloud, time pressure and stress under realistic conditions, exposing weaknesses that solo practice hides, like silence, poor structure or panic.

first_principles.problem: A candidate solves problems easily alone but freezes when someone watches.
truths: Performance under observation differs from solo practice.

analogy.title: A pilot's flight simulator
analogy.story: Engine failures practised dozens of times become routine responses.
analogy.breaks: Simulators replicate physics; mock interviewers vary in quality.

example.title: Four-week mock plan
flow: Week 3: system design mock with senior engineer

check.q: Why aren't solo LeetCode sessions enough?
check.a: They don't train communicating under observation and time pressure, which is what interviews test.

platform-landscape-pramp-vs-the-rest.core: Mock interview options range from free peer platforms (Pramp/Exponent peer mocks) with mutual practice, to paid sessions with experienced interviewers (interviewing.io, Hello Interview, Exponent), to friends and colleagues. Choose by cost, realism, feedback quality and interview type (coding, system design, behavioural).

first_principles.problem: Candidates don't know which platform gives the most useful practice for their stage.

analogy.title: Practising tennis with friends versus a coach
analogy.story: Friends give you volume; a coach spots the flaw in your serve.
analogy.breaks: Tennis coaches stay with you; mock interviewers change every session.

example.title: Budget-aware plan
flow: 2 behavioural mocks with a manager friend

check.q: When are paid expert mocks most valuable?
check.a: Close to real interviews, for calibrated feedback, especially for senior system design rounds.

the-hidden-value-being-the-interviewer.core: Interviewing others, on peer platforms or at work, reveals what interviewers see: how silence feels, how clear structure stands out, and which signals make feedback easy to write. It also builds empathy and pattern recognition, improving your own performance.

first_principles.problem: Candidates don't understand why their 'correct' solutions get lukewarm feedback.
truths: Interviewers judge communication as much as code.

analogy.title: A writer working as an editor
analogy.story: Editing others' drafts teaches you what makes writing clear.
analogy.breaks: Editors see finished drafts; interviewers watch reasoning unfold live.

example.title: Insight from interviewing
flow: As interviewer, had nothing to write
Own next interview: much stronger feedback
example.outcome: interview skills sharpened from the other side.

check.q: What does interviewing others teach about silence?
check.a: It leaves the interviewer with no signal to record, which weakens feedback even if the code is right.

feedback-the-gift-you-must-ask-for.core: Mock interviewers often give polite, vague feedback unless you ask specific questions: 'Would you hire me at senior level? What was my weakest moment? Where did I lose time? What would a strong candidate have done differently?' Record answers and track patterns across sessions.

first_principles.problem: After every mock, the feedback is 'you did fine', which changes nothing.

analogy.title: Asking a doctor for test numbers, not just 'you're fine'
analogy.story: Numbers let you track change and know what to work on.
analogy.breaks: Doctors are obliged to tell you; mock interviewers aren't, so you must ask.

check.q: Why ask a mock interviewer for a hire/no-hire decision?
check.a: It forces a clear judgement, cutting through polite but vague feedback.
